about: Round 4: adversarial verification of 13bff01/abe447a (eight agents plus a critic), 2026-10-21.

results.evidence:
The round-3 plan blocker is fixed: the kill test now starts from a released arm when --table-z is right or missing. The claim's wider part does not hold: "p's retake goes through the same checks" fails after a failed retake, and a mistyped --table-z quietly widens the home region. No new blocker.

Holds (scratch trees q1-new-13bff01 and q1-old-8e226e9; mock flags --probe --orders 1 --table-edge 0.34 --fingertip 0.125, START_Q 0.06,0.18,0.06,1.12,0.10):
- table_top() (brain.py:1064-1067) uses --table-z in every mode, and home_region (brain.py:1074) checks the palm and the fingertips.
- Gate case `released`: on 8e226e9 it gives "result None; no start pose line"; on 13bff01 it gives "result probe; start pose: ... 0.139 rad from home_q ... in the home region".
- Gate case `pause`: fails on old ("order started True, ARM OFF False"), passes on new.
- --table-z 0.075, missing (table top 0.000) and -0.075 all accept the released pose and finish with result probe. -7.5 gives "park refused" and nothing is enabled.
- Start-up order at brain.py:1199-1220 is: read the measured joints, run the region check, enable, check for a mismatch, then plan, keep-out check and move.
- I patched the scratch mock so that a release moves the arm 0.139 rad off home. The p retake then passed: "in the home region (table top 0.075)", Parking., "== ARM ON", result probe.
- FK sweeps of the joint line home (true T 0.075, E 0.33, F 0.125): no torso-band penetration in any configuration. Near home (σ 0.15 rad), 0 of 1887 poses put any corner of the hand box past the edge. With the correct T, no corner of the hand box reaches past the edge within 4 cm below the table top.

Refuted:
(a) A failed retake turns off the checks for the next p. brain.py:589 clears pause_released before park(), so after a failure the next p prints the false line "[p] resumed: the arm is taken back at home". Enter then starts an order whose to_pregrasp calls arms_enable (brain.py:722) with no region check before the enable and no mismatch check.
  - Arm released out of the region: "[p] the arm was not taken back: still paused (ARM OFF)" → "[p] resumed..." → "STUCK: no way home: the arm is away from home with no recorded raise", with 2 enables.
  - Mock enable made to hold a stale pose: "ENABLE MISMATCH ... (0.539 rad apart): released at once", then enable #3 holds the stale pose with no check → "STUCK ... holds at [0.407, 0.199, 0.012]".
(b) --table-z has no range check and is not required (brain.py:92); --table-edge gets edge_arg (brain.py:31).
  - A 1.64 rad overhead pose (palm z 0.624): with --table-z 7.5 or 0.915 it is "in the home region (table top 7.500)" and parked home in joint space. With 0.075 it gives "park refused".
  - The keep-out printed "behind x 0.308". FK of that same line puts a hand-box corner at x 0.341, within 4 cm below the table top, with the edge at 0.33. The mock recorded 0 table contacts, so the overlap is in the FK only.
(c) low_reach (brain.py:1163-1170) uses the wrist, palm and tip points only. From unusual start poses, hand-box corners pass the edge by 0.6-1.6 cm, 15-26 cm below the top: 8 of 1514 at σ 0.3, 17 of 1148 at σ 0.5.
(d) On a mismatch the arm is released with the streamer holding a pose away from home: mock disable_away [[0.429, 0.204, 0.057]]. No gate case exercises this.
results.gate_catches_old_bug:
Yes, for the blocker itself. CHECK_TREE=8e226e9 `released` fails with "result None; no start pose line"; on 13bff01 it gives "result probe". `pause` fails on old and passes on new. The gate cannot see the residuals:
- BASE always passes --table-z 0.075 (check.py:46), so a missing or mistyped T is never tried.
- The mock's disable never moves the arm, so `pause` always retakes from home.
- The mock's enable always takes the measured pose, so ENABLE MISMATCH can never fire.
- No case has a retake that fails and then another p.

residual.issue: Pause/retake: pause_released is cleared before park() runs. After a failed retake ("park refused" or ENABLE MISMATCH), the next p prints "[p] resumed: the arm is taken back at home" while the arm is still OFF. Enter then starts an order whose to_pregrasp (line 722) enables the arm with no region check before the enable and no mismatch check. Reproduced on the instrumented mock: the out-of-region case ended STUCK with the arm enabled away from home; the stale-enable case enabled again with no check. Reachable at every can reset in the kill test and the servo block.
residual.fix: Clear pause_released only after park() succeeds. Alternatively, make every enable with arms_on False (to_pregrasp, assist) go through park()'s pre-enable checks and refuse otherwise. On a failed retake, print 'restart the command' instead of 'p takes it back'. Add a gate case: a failed retake, then p, then Enter → no enable.

residual.issue: --table-z is a bare float with no range check and is not required. A missing value silently becomes 0.0. Centimetres (7.5) or forgetting the 0.84 m subtraction (0.915) makes home_region accept any height. An overhead arm 1.64 rad from home was parked home in joint space; FK puts a hand-box corner at x 0.341 at table-top height (edge 0.33) while the keep-out printed 0.308. In probe mode nothing compares T with the fitted plane.
residual.fix: Add a table_z_arg range check (about -0.25 to 0.20 m), required with motion unless --mock or --dry, like --table-edge. Cap home_region at a joint distance from home_q (about 0.3 rad; releases leave 0.06-0.14). In --probe, compare the fitted plane with T (2 cm), as the air test does.

residual.issue: The keep-out on the joint-space home line (start-up park and p retake) measures only the wrist, palm and tip centre points. The hand box reaches up to about 3.5 cm further forward. From accepted start poses well off home, corners pass the table edge by 0.6-1.6 cm, 15-26 cm below the top: harmless under an open table, a touch on an apron, cabinet or drawer front. Near-home releases are unaffected (0 of 1887).
residual.fix: Use the hand-box corners (the corner set in geom.hand_lowest, with the taped F, H and thickness) in low_reach, as the table floor already does.

residual.issue: ENABLE MISMATCH releases the arm while the streamer holds a pose away from home (mock disable_away), which breaks the 'never released away from home' rule. The check runs after g1-fetch's 2 s enable ramp, so it detects a jump rather than preventing it. The gate never fires it. spikes/scripts/arm_test.py:28 says enable 'holds measured', so the risk is low; behaviour on a re-enable after a release is unverified.
residual.fix: Keep the boot-block reading of ArmStreamer.enable, including re-enable on an existing streamer. On a mismatch, hold (stuck) rather than release. Add an instrumented mock case.

residual.issue: The --table-z help says the tape drives 'the keep-out before a plane is fitted, in every mode'. Outside --air the code uses below=inf (every point counts, x only), which is more conservative than the help says. Documentation mismatch only.
residual.fix: Correct the help text and README.

results.evidence:
Trees extracted to $SCR/q2-{old-8e226e9,new-13bff01,docs-abe447a}. I only instrumented the copy $SCR/q2-inst, where the mock hand's position, size, forearm and appearance time can be set (Q2_* env) and the arm's optical z is printed at each check. Logs are in $SCR/q2-runs/.

What holds:
- The round-3 plan blocker is fixed. Plan :87 and :106-109 now expect a refusal at 10 and 20 cm and "clear" at 30 cm, and state the zone.
- With the 6x8x8 cm mock hand, 0.28 m minimum range, --dry, the code gives what the plan expects:
  - 10 cm: "one region of 17% of the frame has no depth ... valid depth 83%, largest blind region 17%" (blocked).
  - 20 cm: "429 points within 0.30 m".
  - 30 cm: "clear; valid depth 100%, largest blind region 0%".
  - The same holds at slots 12, 09 and 06, and with the arm enabled at home or parked after a release (blocked 17%).
- With a 0.15 or 0.19 m minimum range (D435i at 640x480 / 848x480), 10 and 20 cm are refused by the points rule (1488 and 736 points), 30 cm clear. Flat-hand, stop-gesture and guest-forearm shapes are all refused at 10 and 20 cm.
- Gate: new tree "nearhand ok ... result blocked; ... one region of 17%". 8e226e9: "nearhand FAIL ... result dry; safety (locate): clear; valid depth 83%".

What does not hold on every path:
1. The blind rule is skipped whenever the arm is out: brain.py:460 has `(not self.arms_on or self.at_home_safe())`. So none of the per-segment re-checks run it: high (:739), pre (:744), air steps (:1361), back steps (:1370), approach (:836).
   - Repro: air test (0.38, 0.15) at half speed, with the 10 cm hand appearing after "Reaching.". The log reads "safety (pre): clear; valid depth 83%, largest blind region 17%", the same clear line at all 5 air steps and 5 back steps, then "RESULT order 1: air".
   - The no-motion check runs with the arm disabled, where the rule is on. A "has no depth" pass there therefore says nothing about the arm-out checks, contrary to plan :190-191 ("the no-motion check ... decides what it sees").
   - In the mock, the arm's own centre line in view stays at optical z 0.28-0.43 at every arm-out check (3 air targets, kill, servo). It is not inside a 640x480 minimum range, so the skip is not needed there.
2. The blind region is computed over the whole frame (brain.py:458 `frame.depth[::4, ::4] <= 0`), not over the zone.
   - The camera sits inside the zone volume, so every ray starts in it (100% of pixels). But an invalid pixel has no range, so glare, can lids or black objects at 0.5-1.5 m count the same as a hand at 0.2 m.
   - No depth frames exist under hackathon/spikes (111 JPGs, jsonl, no depth). The only number is "depth 82-97% valid" (spikes/2026-10-19-office-grab.md:6), which does not bound the largest region. The mock models no real invalid depth, so every gate frame reads 0%.
   - From the RGB frames (can lids, a remote, a laptop) I would guess 1-3%, but that is unmeasured. If it is 8% or more, plan :87/:108 stops the session at the no-motion block (fail-safe, no motion).
3. 20 cm sits on the zone boundary. A hand whose near edge is at x 0.30 still gives 269 points; at x 0.31 it reads "clear". The plan itself gives the zone as 17-22 cm from the chest (geom.py:22 says the chest is at 0.13, the STL bands at belly height say 0.063-0.080, geom.py:273-275).
4. The no-motion command uses --orders 4. Blocked orders count (brain.py:1234, :1466), so the hand test uses 2-3 of the 4 orders.

Nothing found can cause unsafe motion. Items 2 and 3 can end the session early, before any motion.
results.gate_catches_old_bug:
Yes for the narrow case. Running `CHECK_TREE=<8e226e9 tree> check.py --cases nearhand` gives "nearhand FAIL 12.4s result dry; safety (locate): clear; valid depth 83%, 0 points in the zone". On 13bff01 it gives "nearhand ok 11.8s result blocked; safety (locate): one region of 17% of the frame has no depth".

The gate only covers part of the claim:
- It runs only --dry (arm off), so it never reaches the arm-out re-checks, where the rule is switched off.
- It runs only on mock frames with a 0% baseline blind region, so it cannot catch a false refusal on real D435i frames.
- It places a single hand at 10 cm, so the 20/30 cm boundary is untested.

residual.issue: The blind-region check (brain.py:458-461) counts invalid depth anywhere in the frame: glare, can lids, black objects, the floor. Its real baseline is unmeasured: no depth frames exist under hackathon/spikes, and the only figure is '82-97% valid' (office-grab.md:6), which does not bound the largest region. The mock always reads 0%. If the real largest region is 8% or more, every locate refuses (dry run, air, kill, servo), and the plan's stop rule ends the session at the no-motion block with no data. This is fail-safe (no motion), but the plan can then answer nothing.
residual.fix: Record MM in the boot or dry run with nothing in front and save the depth frame. If MM is 8 or more, read bundle_locate_depth.png. If the region is a far surface, remove or cover the object, or run with --blind-max set to MM + 0.05 as a logged deviation, instead of stopping. Add blind_max to CALIB_ARGS and the order params: today an override is not logged (brain.py:1237, CALIB_ARGS). Better still, refuse on growth over a start-up baseline mask.

residual.issue: With the arm out, the blind rule is skipped, so none of the per-segment re-checks run it (high :739, pre :744, air :1361, back :1370, approach :836). Mock air test with a 10 cm hand inside a 0.28 m minimum range appearing after 'Reaching.': 'safety (pre): clear; valid depth 83%, largest blind region 17%', the same at all 5 air and 5 back steps, and the order completes. The plan (:190-191) says the no-motion check 'decides what it sees', but that check runs with the arm off, where the rule is on, and the plan accepts 'has no depth' as a pass. In the mock, the arm's centre line in view stays at optical z 0.28 or more at every arm-out check, so the skip is not needed at 640x480. Not a blocker: at 640x480 the 10 cm hand has valid depth and the points rule refuses it (1488 points), and a guest forearm adds points (112 even at a 0.28 m minimum range).
residual.fix: Keep the blind rule on with the arm out, after masking the arm's projected silhouette (the arm_segments already used for `own`, projected with radius plus margin) out of `inval`. Or require the 10 cm no-motion refusal to read 'within 0.30 m'; if it reads 'has no depth', write in the plan that the arm-out checks cannot see a hand there.

residual.issue: The 20 cm expectation sits on the zone boundary. Mock: a hand near edge at x 0.30 gives 269 points (refused); at x 0.31 it reads 'clear'. The plan gives the zone as 17-22 cm from the chest (geom.py:22 'chest front ~0.13'; STL bands at belly height 0.063-0.080, geom.py:273-275). If the tape starts at a strap or the stand, or the fingertips end up past 22 cm, 20 cm reads clear and the stop rule at :107 ends the session before any motion.
residual.fix: Test at 10 and 15 cm (pelvis x 0.18 and 0.23) and expect a refusal; keep 30 cm as clear. Or measure the 20 cm hand from the torso shell at belly height and accept either result at 20 cm.

residual.issue: The no-motion command runs --orders 4 with 'Enter per slot' for 4 slots, plus a hand test of 10, 20 and 30 cm 'at one slot'. Each hand position is a separate order, and blocked orders count (brain.py:1234 counts every order, :1466 stops at --orders), so only about 2 of the 4 slots, possibly not including the edge-probe slot, are located before the run ends.
residual.fix: Use --orders 6, or run the hand test as its own --dry command.

residual.issue: A stale line under 'Round 2 plan changes' still reads 'a hand held at 20 and 30 cm (must be refused)'. This contradicts the plan, which now expects clear at 30 cm, and HANDOFF :24.
residual.fix: Mark the line as superseded by round 3, or update it.

residual.issue: At the cross-body air target (0.40, -0.08), the robot's forearm is inside the zone: 365-445 zone points are excluded as own-arm at pre, air and back. A guest's hand within 7-8 cm of the forearm there is not counted. Also, if g1-fetch ever returns NaN for invalid depth, `<= 0` counts NaN as valid for the blind rule while geom.py:220 (`> 0`) counts it as invalid.
residual.fix: Keep people out of the zone during motion, as the plan already says. Use `~(depth > 0)` for the blind mask.

results.evidence:
All work was in scratch copies: qs-old-8e226e9, qs-new-13bff01, qs-docs-abe447a, plus qs-inst-13bff01, where two lines in stuck_loop were changed so a pty can type the keys. The repo is unchanged: git status shows the same 3 untracked files. Logs are in $SCR/qs-logs/*.log.

WHAT HOLDS (13bff01)
- q, Ctrl-C or SIGTERM while stuck only set quit_after_home (brain.py:323-326). on_signal does not raise while stuck, retreating, quitting or shutting down (1458). check_abort never raises Abort while retreating (312). stuck_loop clears freeze_req before y (444).
- run_retreat turns every Exception into stuck (1157). Shutdown re-enters stuck_loop after any failure and catches BaseException (1405-1415).
- The four gate cases pass on 13bff01 and fail on 8e226e9 with this mock.
- The pty runs used the real stdin key thread: SIGTERM x2 while stuck prints "[ctrl-c] the arm is stuck and holding ..." and nothing moves.
- Plan step 4 on the idle loop (run H): "[q] stop: the arm holds where it is", the next h+y gets home, then "the arm is home: quitting as asked".
- Unknown lines get "not a key ...".

WHAT BREAKS
1. quit! does not always mean no motion.
   - Run D, the plan's air-test contact case: --air --speed 0.5 --orders 1, a failure injected at the 5th target after "Sliding.", and quit! typed right after "I could not complete that reach.". Output: "[quit!] exiting WITHOUT moving or releasing the arm ..." / "== RECOVER retreat" / "SAY: Up and back." ... "SAY: Home." / "== quit!: the arm is at home". 901 targets were streamed after the failure.
   - Cause: quit! sets freeze_req only while retreating (337-340), and recover_fast opens the hand (0.8 s plus the open wait, 1225) before the retreat starts.
   - Run F2, real key thread: "y\nquit!\n" typed together while stuck. quit! was acknowledged, then the whole way out ran: back, bridge, home. stuck_loop never re-checks force_quit after the y wait (440-444).
2. A second stop is not always honoured (plan 146-148, README:42, the console line at 330).
   - Run B, q then a typed at once: "[a] aborting this order", then 394 targets home and "Releasing my arm.". The a sets abort (327) and shutdown clears it (1402).
   - Run A2, real key thread: a second q 20 ms after "Moving my arm back before I stop." printed "[q] second stop: the arm holds where it is instead of coming home", then home and released. hold_on_quit is read only once (1407), before the say and plan_retreat. Run A is the same through SAYKEYS: 394 targets.
   - Run C: a, then q,q before the recovery retreat starts. "second stop" was printed, the arm went home and was released.
3. The key reader can die, leaving no h, y or quit!.
   - Run G: Ctrl-D while stuck. h and quit! got no answer; Ctrl-C and SIGTERM only re-printed the stuck text; the reminder kept going until my driver used SIGKILL (rc -9).
   - Run F1: "o stage=pre note=x" typed during the probe gave "Exception in thread Thread-1 (keys) ... TypeError: OrderLog.event() got multiple values for keyword argument 'stage'" (358). After that, q and h were ignored.
4. Run E, pause: a stop during the p-resume park printed "STUCK: stopped during the retreat (Frozen)", then "[p] the arm was not taken back: still paused (ARM OFF)" (590) while the arm was enabled.
5. Run F6, startup: SIGINT during the enable left disables at 0: no release, and "arm service on -> 0" ran with the streamer still on. g1-fetch's enable is a 2 s ramp per spikes/scripts/arm_test.py.
6. Run F4: SIGHUP has no handler. rc -1, no shutdown, no stats.

'HOLDS' AND PROCESS EXIT
- "Holds" means g1-fetch's streamer thread keeps re-publishing the last target; the brain sends nothing while stuck. The main thread cannot finish without shutdown, which loops while the arm is away from home.
- The process ends without shutdown only on SIGHUP, SIGKILL, SIGQUIT, OOM or a native crash.
- What the G1 does when arm_sdk stops (kill -9) is unknown. g1-docs 05_01 documents only the explicit weight ramp (lines 178-193). g1-fetch arm.py is not in the repo (HANDOFF:118). Also unknown: whether the streamer thread is a daemon (if not, quit! may hang at exit) and whether g1-fetch has an atexit or close hook that ramps the weight to 0 (that would release the arm away from home).
results.gate_catches_old_bug:
Yes for what the four cases test. On 13bff01 all pass:
- qstuck: "ended 0.0 from home ... quit after home: True"
- wayfail and wayfail1: "0 targets before the next way out"
- secondq: "1 targets"

With CHECK_TREE=8e226e9 all fail:
- qstuck: "ended 0.4427 from home ... quit after home: False"
- wayfail: "316 targets before the next way out"
- wayfail1: "ended 0.439 from home"
- secondq: "405 targets"

The mock types every key synchronously at a target or a sentence, so the gate never sees:
- a second q, a or Ctrl-C after shutdown's hold check, or before an in-order recovery retreat
- q and a typed together
- quit! before an automatic retreat, or right after y
- the stdin thread itself (EOF, exceptions)
- signals during enable, and SIGHUP

residual.issue: quit! is honoured for motion only while stuck or already retreating. Typed in the 1-2 s between a SKILL FAILED and the start of the recovery retreat, it prints 'exiting WITHOUT moving or releasing the arm' and the whole retreat still streams. Run D, the plan's air-test contact rule (L2+B, then quit!): 901 targets after the failure, then '== quit!: the arm is at home'. The same happens after 'Order cancelled.'. y and quit! typed together (run F2, real key thread) also run the whole way out, because stuck_loop does not re-check force_quit after the y wait (443-444). There is still no damping check (HANDOFF:149 defers it, but quit! is this plan's exit).
residual.fix: Make check_abort raise Frozen whenever force_quit is set, in every state including retreating. Check force_quit before recover_fast starts a retreat and after the y wait. Read loco.fsm_id() and refuse quit! unless the robot is in damping. Gate: an air run with 'Sliding.;fail;5' and SAYKEYS 'I could not complete that reach.:quit!' must stream 0 targets after the quit!.

residual.issue:
The second stop is not always honoured, although plan 146-148, README:42 and the console ('a second q or a stops it there') promise it. Three cases:
- q then a typed at once: the a only sets abort (327), shutdown clears it (1402), and the arm went home (run B, 394 targets).
- A second q or Ctrl-C after the single hold_on_quit check at 1407 but before run_retreat sets retreating (the say plus plan_retreat): it prints 'second stop: the arm holds' and the arm goes home and is released (run A2, real key thread, q 20 ms after 'Moving my arm back').
- q,q before an in-order recovery retreat (after 'Order cancelled.' or a SKILL FAILED): the same message, then home (run C).
The motion is the planned, keep-out-checked retreat, and the plan names L2+B as the only stop, so this is not a blocker.
residual.fix: While an automatic way home runs without a y, have check_abort raise Frozen once hold_on_quit is set, and treat an a after a q as a second stop. Gate cases: SAYKEYS 'Moving my arm back before I stop.:q', keys:q+a, and 'Order cancelled.:q+q'.

residual.issue: The stdin reader thread has no guard. Ctrl-D (EOF) ends it silently (run G). An o line with stage=, ev= or tag= during an order raises a TypeError at 358 and kills it (run F1). After that, h, y, q and quit! get no answer. While stuck, Ctrl-C and SIGTERM only set quit_after_home, so the only exit is kill -9, whose effect on the robot is unknown. The plan has no procedure for a live brain whose keys are dead.
residual.fix: Wrap key() in try/except inside keys(). On EOF, reopen /dev/tty or print a loud warning and give another way to quit! (for example a second SIGTERM while stuck). Namespace the obs keys. Add 'keys not answered' to the plan's stuck procedure: L2+B, then kill the PID.

residual.issue: A stop or refusal during the p-resume park (Taking my arm. / Parking.) leaves the arm enabled and stuck, yet the console prints '[p] the arm was not taken back: still paused (ARM OFF)' (run E: the STUCK line, then this line). The plan's can-reset rule keys on ARM OFF.
residual.fix: Print ARM OFF only when arms_on is False. When stuck, print and say the stuck guidance instead.

residual.issue: Ctrl-C or SIGTERM during g1-fetch's 2 s enable ramp (startup park or p-resume) raises Abort inside rb.arms.enable() before arms_on is set. Shutdown then skips arms_disable and switches the arm service on while the streamer may still be enabled and the weight half ramped (run F6: disables 0, 'arm service on -> 0'). The plan's own start-pose check (stop if more than 1 cm off) invites a Ctrl-C at exactly this moment. The arm is at the side, so the motion risk is small.
residual.fix: Set arms_on (or an 'enabling' flag) before calling enable, and in shutdown always disable a streamer that may be on. Alternatively, have on_signal only set quit, never raise, while arms_on or enabling.

residual.issue: Process death skips shutdown. SIGHUP has no handler: tmux kill-pane or kill-session ends the brain at once with the arm out (run F4: rc -1, no '== shutting down'), the same as kill -9 or the OOM killer. What the G1 does when arm_sdk stops is unknown: g1-docs 05_01 documents only the explicit weight ramp, and g1-fetch arm.py is not in the repo. Also unknown: whether the streamer thread is a daemon (if not, quit! hangs at exit with the streamer still publishing) and whether g1-fetch registers an atexit or close hook that ramps the weight to 0 (that would release the arm away from home after quit!). The race from round 3 is unchanged: a Ctrl-C between run_retreat's retreating=False and set_stuck's stuck assignment (410-411, under a millisecond) raises Abort, and shutdown then homes the arm with no y.
residual.fix: Add SIGHUP to the handled signals. In the boot block, also read whether the streamer thread is a daemon and look for atexit/close hooks in arm.py, and write down what the controller does when arm_sdk stops. Assign stuck before clearing retreating.

residual.issue:
The plan's stuck procedure differs from the code in these places:
- A q or Ctrl-C during the way out also quits after the next way out reaches home (322; run H). Step 4 says this only for q while stuck, and the console at that moment says only 'h, then y, brings it home later'.
- A plain quit during a running way out or the shutdown retreat only prints help, and the motion continues (341; run I: the way out completed and 3 more orders ran). The spoken line 'then type quit' invites exactly this.
- After a SKILL FAILED the brain opens the hand and retreats home by itself (recover_fast); the air-test and kill-test stop rules (115-120) do not say the arm will move.
- y is never acknowledged, and a y typed before 'Press y' is discarded.
- 'Turning my wrist.' is said for any bridge over 5 degrees, while describe_retreat may name the shoulder or the elbow.
- A q that lands after a retreat's last target sets quit_after_home and freeze_req but not quit, so the session continues.
residual.fix: After the code fixes, rewrite steps 4-6 and the SKILL FAILED rules key by key: what moves by itself and what stops it. Accept quit like quit! whenever the arm is out, print '[y] running the way out', and say 'Turning my <joint>'.

results.evidence:
Scratch only. Trees: $SCR/q4-{old-8e226e9,new-13bff01,docs-abe447a}. Instrumented copy: $SCR/q4-inst (mock only). It adds a configurable true hand box (BRAIN_MOCK_HANDBOX), an exact box-over-table contact (BRAIN_MOCK_EXACT: the corners over the table plus the box edges cut by x = edge), frictionless sliding contact (BRAIN_MOCK_SLIDE) and per-phase penetration of the true hand. Logs: $SCR/q4-logs/s1..s10 ($SCR = /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-junda-robot-harness/44b035f1-dc0d-4025-a748-1eab1915cdb8/scratchpad).

WHAT HOLDS
- The floor follows the hand box through the predicted arrival pose: motion.py:56-79, geom.py:283-288.

That stop line feeds forward the sag measured at the high waypoint, 12 cm higher and with forearm pitch about -16 deg instead of +5 to -10 deg. So the check really tests whether sag(high) - sag(stop) in z exceeds 6 mm. It runs in air run 1 (0.38, 0.15), air run 4 and at every kill slot. In the mock this 'held' value was only 0.0002-0.0008, because the mock arm has no friction or hysteresis (mock_robot.py:381-383). That ends the air test (plan :115, no kill test) or every kill block (plan :118). 'held' is printed only when it refuses, so the air runs cannot show how close it came before the kill test. This is distinct from q4's :189 item, though q4's 'corr_tol' note may overlap.
